title: 第三章 交货第四章 县城立足
lines: 三天后，沈南枝把二十件饰品整整齐齐码在篮子里，用一块干净蓝布盖上，背上珠珠出了门。
这三天她几乎没合眼。
第一天去县城小商品市场进货，玛瑙珠子、铜丝、银钩子、绒布，花了一百三十块，心疼得直抽气。第二天和第三天从早坐到晚，手指被钳子磨出两个水泡，她用针挑了，贴块布条继续干。珠珠就蹲在旁边看，有时候帮她递珠子，安安静静的，不吵不闹。
二十件做完，她还多做了五件备用的。
桂姨的杂货铺在县城东街，门面不大，门口挂着“桂香杂货铺”的木板招牌，漆掉了一半。桂姨正在门口扫地，看见她来了，扫把一扔就迎上来。
“来了来了，快进来坐。”
沈南枝没坐，直接把篮子放在柜台上，掀开蓝布。
桂姨拿起一串项链凑到窗口光底下看。深蓝色和银色的珠子串的，中间坠一颗水滴形蓝石头，下面用铜丝绕了两个小圈。她翻来覆去看了好一会儿，又拿起一对耳环，对着光瞧了瞧接口，又拽了拽。
“行。”桂姨笑着点头，“这批货我要了。多少钱来着？”
“耳环三块，手链四块，项链七块。二十件，一共九十。上次您给了十块定金，再给我八十。”
桂姨从抽屉里拿出算盘噼里啪啦打了一阵，数出八十块钱递过来。票子旧，有的缺了角，但钱就是钱。
沈南枝接了，没数第二遍，直接揣进兜里。
桂姨看她这爽快劲，笑了：“你这姑娘，跟外面传的不一样啊。”
沈南枝也笑：“外面传我什么样？”
桂姨咳了一声，没接话。
沈南枝知道外面传她什么样——泼妇、懒婆娘、贼、不要脸。她不在乎。
“桂姨，这批货您试着卖。要是好卖，我下批还能做。您想要什么款式跟我说，我给您专门设计。”
“专门设计？”桂姨眨眨眼，“你还懂设计？”
“懂一点，瞎琢磨的。”
桂姨看了她一眼，没再多问。转身从货架上拿了两包饼干塞给珠珠：“给孩子吃的，拿着。”
珠珠看了看沈南枝，沈南枝点了头，她才接过去，小声说了句“谢谢奶奶”。桂姨笑得眼睛眯成一条缝。
从杂货铺出来，沈南枝没急着回去。她带着珠珠在县城逛了一圈，看了供销社的柜台和街边摆摊的饰品——款式老气，颜色暗沉，最贵的卖四块五，跟她做的东西没法比。心里有了底，她又去了趟邮局，买了十个邮票十个信封，花了三块六。她打算等生意再大一点，就往省城的批发市场寄样品。
从邮局出来，在路边摊吃了一碗馄饨。珠珠把汤都喝光了，碗底朝天。
吃完她又去了小商品市场，补了一批货——珠子、铜丝、钳子、绒布，花了一百五十多。兜里剩下的钱不多了，但够用。
回去的路上，珠珠没睡着，趴在她背上叽叽喳喳说话，说桂姨家的饼干好吃，说馄饨好吃，说县城比村里好玩。沈南枝有一搭没一搭地应着，嘴里嗯嗯啊啊，其实腿已经快断了。
回到村里，天还没黑。
她刚走到家门口，就看见门锁被人动过了。
锁还是那把锁，但位置不对。她走的时候锁头朝下，现在锁头朝上，歪着挂在门鼻上。
沈南枝把珠珠放下来，蹲下跟她平视：“珠珠，你在这等着，妈妈先进去看看，没叫你别进来。”
珠珠点了点头，抱着布娃娃站到一边。
沈南枝开了锁，推门进去。屋里跟她走的时候差不多，床上的被子叠得整整齐齐，灶台上的碗筷摆得规规矩矩。但空气里有股陌生的味道——不是她用的那种肥皂味，是另一种，带点甜腻腻的香，像雪花膏。
她走到床边蹲下来看床底下。她走之前在床底下的地面上撒了一层薄薄的灰——前世在书上看过的法子，有人进过屋子，灰上就会有脚印。
灰上确实有脚印。不大不小，不像男人的鞋印，倒像是女人的布鞋印。脚印从门口一直延伸到墙根，在墙根那里停留了很久，地上有来回走动的痕迹。
墙根那里，就是她藏布包的地方。
沈南枝伸手摸了摸那块墙皮，泥巴还是湿的——有人摸过这里，但没找到东西，又把泥巴糊回去了。
content_en:
Three days later, Shen Nanzhi neatly packed the twenty pieces of jewelry in the basket, covered it with a clean blue cloth, and went out with beads on his back.
She had barely slept for the past three days.
On the first day, I went to the county small commodity market to purchase agate beads, copper wire, silver hooks, and flannel. I spent 130 yuan, and I was so distressed that I gasped. On the second and third days, she sat from morning to night, and two blisters were produced on her fingers by the pliers. She picked them out with a needle, put a piece of cloth on them and continued to work. Zhuzhu squatted nearby and watched, sometimes helping her pass the beads, quietly and without making any noise.
Twenty pieces were finished, and she made five more as spares.
Aunt Gui's grocery store is on the east street of the county town. It has a small front. There is a wooden signboard of "Guixiang Grocery Store" hanging at the door, with half of the paint peeled off. Aunt Gui was sweeping the floor at the door. When she saw her coming, she threw the broom and rushed towards her.
"Come on, come on, come in and sit down."
Shen Nanzhi didn't sit down, just put the basket on the counter and lifted the blue cloth.
Aunt Gui picked up a necklace and looked at it under the light of the window. It is strung with dark blue and silver beads, with a drop-shaped blue stone hanging in the middle, and two small circles wrapped with copper wire below. She looked over and over for a while, then picked up a pair of earrings, looked at the connection against the light, and tugged again.
"Okay." Aunt Gui smiled and nodded, "I want this batch of goods. How much does it cost?"
"Three yuan for earrings, four yuan for bracelets, and seven yuan for necklaces. Twenty pieces, totaling ninety. Last time you gave me a deposit of ten yuan, so give me another eighty."
Aunt Gui took out the abacus from the drawer and crackled it for a while, then counted out eighty yuan and handed it over. The bills are old and some are missing corners, but money is money.
Shen Nanzhi took it and put it directly into his pocket without counting the second time.
Aunt Gui saw her cheerfulness and smiled: "You girl, you are different from what is said outside."
Shen Nanzhi also laughed: "What do you think of me outside?"
Aunt Gui coughed and didn't answer.
Shen Nanzhi knew what the outside world said about her - a shrew, a lazy woman, a thief, and a shameless person. She doesn't care.
"Aunt Gui, you try to sell this batch of goods. If it sells well, I can make the next batch. Tell me what style you want, and I will design it specially for you."
"Specialized in design?" Aunt Gui blinked, "Do you still know about design?"
"I know a little bit, but I'm just thinking about it."
Aunt Gui glanced at her and didn't ask any more questions. He turned around and took two packs of biscuits from the shelf and gave them to Zhuzhu: "Here are the food for the children."
Zhuzhu looked at Shen Nanzhi, and Shen Nanzhi nodded before she took it and whispered "Thank you, grandma." Aunt Gui smiled until her eyes narrowed into slits.
After coming out of the grocery store, Shen Nanzhi was in no hurry to go back. She took Zhuzhu around the county town, looking at the counters of the supply and marketing cooperatives and the jewelry at street stalls - the styles were old-fashioned, the colors were dull, and the most expensive ones sold for four and a half yuan, which was incomparable to the things she made. Feeling confident, she went to the post office again and bought ten stamps and ten envelopes for three and a half yuan. She plans to send samples to wholesale markets in provincial capitals when her business grows.
After coming out of the post office, I ate a bowl of wontons at a roadside stall. Zhuzhu drank up all the soup and turned the bottom of the bowl upward.
After eating, she went to the small commodity market and replenished a batch of goods - beads, copper wire, pliers, flannel, which cost more than one hundred and fifty. There isn't much money left in my pocket, but it's enough.
On the way back, Zhuzhu didn't fall asleep. She lay on her back and chattered, saying that Aunt Gui's biscuits were delicious, that the wontons were delicious, and that the county town was more fun than the village. Shen Nanzhi responded one after another, umming in his mouth, but in fact his leg was almost broken.
When we got back to the village, it was still dark.
As soon as she walked to the door of her home, she saw that the door lock had been moved.
The lock was still the same, but in the wrong position. When she left, the lock was facing down, but now it was facing up, hanging crookedly on the nose of the door.
Shen Nanzhi put Zhuzhu down, squatted down and looked at her levelly: "Zhuzhu, wait here. Mom will go in first and take a look. Don't come in unless I tell you."
Zhuzhu nodded and stood aside holding the doll.
Shen Nanzhi unlocked the door and pushed in. The room was much the same as when she left, the quilt on the bed was neatly folded, and the dishes and chopsticks on the stove were arranged in an orderly manner. But there was a strange smell in the air - not the soap she used, but another kind, with a sweet and greasy fragrance, like cream.
She walked to the bed and knelt down to look under the bed. Before she left, she spread a thin layer of ashes on the ground under the bed - a method she had read in a book in her previous life. If someone entered the house, there would be footprints on the ashes.
There were indeed footprints in the ashes. Not too big, not too small, not like a man's shoe print, but more like a woman's cloth shoe print. The footprints extended from the door to the base of the wall, where they stayed for a long time, and there were traces of walking back and forth on the ground.
The base of the wall was where she hid her cloth bag.
Shen Nanzhi reached out and touched the wall. The mud was still wet - someone had touched here before, but didn't find anything and put the mud back again.
title_en: Chapter 3 Delivery Chapter 4 Establishment in the County
